paper_title: Stepping Up Superradiance Constraints on Axions
coupling_convention: y-axis plotted as 1/f_a in GeV^-1 (inverse axion decay constant); x-axis is m_a in eV. Values emitted exactly as plotted, no inversion to f_a performed.
notes: Paper (arXiv:2412.03655, Witte & Mummery) derives new 95% CI (2-sigma) black hole superradiance constraints on the axion decay constant f_a vs axion mass m_a using spins of solar-mass black holes (Cyg X-1 conservative + GRS 1915+105), evolving all superradiant states with n<=5 with fully relativistic self-interaction rates. Primary result is Fig. 1 in the f_a-m_a plane, hence AxionMass. The paper claims ~1 order of magnitude improvement in f_a sensitivity over prior limits (Ref. [44]) and extension to higher masses via m=2 spin-down. The exclusion is an astrophysical (not DM haloscope) bound, so no local DM density assumed. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: no numerical table of the exclusion boundary is provided in the text; the data_points above are approximate reconstructions of the Fig. 1 dark-blue fiducial exclusion boundary based on the stated black hole masses (M~22 M_sun, alpha~0.1-0.5 implying m_a ~ few x 1e-13 to ~1e-11 eV, with example mu=2e-12 eV) and stated order-of-magnitude improvement over previous f_a ~ 1e15 GeV limits.
